tier_reason: The only opened numbers come from a rival TSDB author's one-off wiki shootout (TickTock wins it, IoTDB also beats TDengine) on a modified fork of IoTDB-benchmark (ytyou/iotdb-benchmark, public), with the CPU model and Docker image versions stated but prebuilt images and unequal per-database workloads; per the xan, winnow and FEX precedents a competitor's shootout is not a well-known independent suite, so C rather than B. TDengine's own TSBS reports on tdengine.com are vendor evidence (C) and could not be opened (EGRESS_BLOCKED).

corrections.caveats: Numbers come from a third-party wiki written by the author of a rival time-series database (TickTock), who wins the same chart; Apache IoTDB (1,495,065 datapoint/s) also beats TDengine there, so TDengine is only faster than InfluxDB, TimescaleDB and OpenTSDB. The TDengine, InfluxDB and TimescaleDB figures are read from the wiki's result images (througput_w.jpg and througput_tbl.jpg in the ylin30/ticktock-wiki repo, both opened and matching); the table header is cropped ('Throughput(Da...'), so the read rows' unit is not certain. Old versions (TDengine 2.0.22.0 from the 2.x line, InfluxDB 2.0, TimescaleDB latest-pg12 reported as 2.6.0) on a laptop with a 5400 RPM HDD, each database in a 2-vCPU, 4 GB Docker container with the benchmark client on the same machine. Workloads were not equal: TimescaleDB ran 10 clients x 10 devices x 100 sensors (write batch 100 instead of 10, which the wiki itself calls unfair to the others), and TDengine ran 1M loops versus 100K for InfluxDB and TimescaleDB. The harness is the TickTock author's fork of IoTDB-benchmark (github.com/ytyou/iotdb-benchmark, public) with connection pools added to the InfluxDB 2.0, TDengine and OpenTSDB clients; its README lists a TDengine 2.2.0.2 adaptor while the run used the 2.0.22.0 image. TDengine's own TSBS reports on tdengine.com (blocked here, search snippet only) claim ingestion 1.5x to 6.7x faster than TimescaleDB and 3.0x to 10.6x faster than InfluxDB, using the public taosdata/tsbs fork (scripts/tsdbComp); these are vendor numbers. The arXiv paper 'Benchmarking Specialized Databases for High-frequency Data' (2301.12561) is, per search snippets, a benchmark of ClickHouse, InfluxDB, kdb+ and TimescaleDB, so the earlier claim that it reports TDengine at 1.63M rows/s could not be confirmed and should not be relied on.

notes: All claimed write, read and memory figures match the wiki text and its images exactly; downgraded B to C because the measurement is a competitor's one-off shootout with unequal workloads (TimescaleDB batch 100, TDengine 10x more loops), old versions and prebuilt images. Shortcomings to record: rival-run shootout where TickTock and IoTDB beat TDengine; unequal per-database workload shapes; 2.x-era versions on an HDD laptop; vendor TSBS reports unopened. Category columnar-analytics is a better fit than the assignment's message-queues-logs; metadata (25.2k stars, AGPL-3.0, last commit 2026-09-02 on main, 730k running instances in README) confirmed.

tier_reason: First-party VectorDBBench run published in the project's docs repo (zvec-ai/zvec-web content/docs/en/db/benchmarks.mdx plus chart SVGs) with reproduction commands, but no CPU model or build flags (prebuilt PyPI wheel), and the rival rows are VectorDBBench's stored standard results measured by Zilliz on other hardware, so C.

corrections.hardware: Alibaba Cloud ECS g9i.4xlarge (16 vCPU, 64 GiB RAM); the docs recommend Ubuntu 24.04 for reproduction; CPU model not named. The Milvus and Zilliz Cloud rows are VectorDBBench standard results, which the VectorDBBench README says were generated by a client on an 8-core, 32 GB host with an Intel Xeon Platinum 8375C at 2.90 GHz (open-source servers on the same processor type), so Zvec and its rivals were not measured on the same machine.
corrections.caveats: First-party numbers. The docs site zvec.org was not opened; the figures were read from the PNG charts embedded in the SVGs of the zvec-ai/zvec-web docs repo (qps-10M.svg, recall-10M.svg, load-duration-10M.svg, qps-1M.svg, recall-1M.svg) and the reproduction steps from content/docs/en/db/benchmarks.mdx in the same repo. The rival rows are VectorDBBench's stored standard results (vectordb_bench/results has Milvus, ZillizCloud and other directories but no Zvec results), measured by Zilliz with a client-server path on Xeon Platinum 8375C hosts, while Zvec ran in-process on an Alibaba g9i.4xlarge, so hardware and deployment differ. Not iso-recall: Zvec recall is 0.9328 (10M) and 0.9164 (1M) versus 0.951 and 0.9528 for Milvus sq8 and 0.9843 and 0.9799 for Milvus HNSW, so the 19x to 47x Milvus ratios partly buy lower recall. At matched recall the fairer comparisons are Zilliz Cloud 8cu (recall 0.932 vs 0.9328 on 10M, 0.9169 vs 0.9164 on 1M), about 2.1x and 1.7x QPS (derived from page data), and on 10M QdrantCloud-16c64g-1.14.1 (recall 0.9357, 446.9 QPS), about 19x (derived from page data). Milvus versions are mixed (2.2.12 and 2.5.11). Zvec version is v0.1.1 (PyPI upload 2026-01-28); the current release is v0.7.0. The README embeds only a QPS chart. FAISS is not in this comparison. CPU model not stated, so not tier A.

notes: Every claimed QPS, recall and load-duration figure matches the chart images exactly; tier C confirmed. Shortcomings to record: first-party run on different hardware from the VectorDBBench rival rows (Xeon Platinum 8375C, client-server) with no CPU model; not iso-recall versus Milvus (Zvec 0.93/0.92 vs 0.95-0.98), only Zilliz Cloud matches recall (2.1x/1.7x); measured on v0.1.1. Metadata confirmed (Apache-2.0, 16.1k stars, last commit 2026-09-29); the 'built on Proxima' part of stars_or_usage is not stated in the README or docs index I opened (left uncorrected).
